messages:
Aisha: quick idea — propose we try 'sparse cohorting' for traces/metrics to reduce cardinality for cost attribution without losing per-tenant economics. thoughts?

Tyler: explain the core of it? sounds like bucketing? :thinking:

Aisha: yes, bucket traces into stable cohorts (hash-based) instead of carrying full high-cardinality attrs everywhere. then attribute cost at cohort-level and stitch to tenants offline for billing queries. tradeoffs: approximation vs raw cardinality blowup.

Maya: curious how this affects query accuracy. do we lose the ability to get exact token-level cost for a single request?

Aisha: short answer: exact per-request cost still recorded for a sample set + metadata to reconstruct where needed. primary path is approximate but bounded error; we keep deterministic mapping so same request -> same cohort.

Jin: how do cohorts map to routing/caching? if cohort buckets mix multiple models/seq-lens we could mis-estimate latency/cost.

Aisha: good point. plan is multi-key cohorting: cohort_id = hash(tenant_id||model_id||input_len_bucket) % N. that keeps similar shapes together. also allow dynamic N per region.

Ben (sre): operational concerns: cohort count = new cardinality factor. need to make sure ingest pipeline can handle a change (increase/decrease) without reassigning historical cohorts. prefer power-of-two stable buckets, and expose a migration plan.

Aisha: agreed. using stable hash + epoched cohort namespace. older data remains queryable under its epoch id. new epoch with different N doesn't mutate existing cohort ids.

Elena (product): what's the UX for customers who want exact usage vs approximate? can we surface cohort confidence and fall back to sampled exact accounting?

Aisha: yes — two-tier billing UX: default = cohorted aggregated invoice with small bounded delta; enterprise opt-in = full exact accounting via full-trace retention & lookups (or charge for full retention). we'll show confidence band in Console.

Tyler: show me a tiny assignment snippet so I can think about implementation constraints.

Aisha: here's a simple pseudo example we used in the spike:

```
# python-ish
key = f"{tenant_id}:{model_id}:{min(seq_len,1024)//32}"
cohort = murmurhash64(key, seed=epoch) % cohort_count
emit(trace, attrs={"cohort_id": str(epoch)+"-"+str(cohort)})
```

Aisha: ingest side writes cohort_id into trace envelope; downstream aggregator stores cost-per-cohort-per-model-per-window.

Jin: what about late enrichment? if billing key is missing at edge, cohorting would still need tenant hint to avoid mixing customers.

Aisha: fallback: cohorting prefers tenant_id if present; if missing we place into anonymized-spill cohorts and track a small mapping hop to final tenant once billing lookup completes. this preserves safety but adds some deferred attribution.

Ben (sre): retention: aggregated cohort metrics can be kept longer at low cardinality. raw traces for full accounting kept only for sampled set or enterprise customers. helps storage costs. :+1:

ingest-bot: deploy scheduled: cohort-spike feature branch -> staging at 2026-04-02T03:00Z

Maya: queryability — need helper functions to expand cohort -> sample traces for a tenant. also add a QA dashboard showing cohort homogeneity (latency/cost variance).

Aisha: yes, plan: automated cohort-health job that flags high-variance cohorts and suggests split keys (e.g., split by model or seq_len finer bucket).

Elena (product): can this power smarter autoscaling? if cohorts predict higher token churn we could pre-scale dedicated pools per cohort class. new product idea.

Aisha: exactly — cohorts are useful beyond billing: routing, pre-warming caches, quantization profiles per-cohort.

Tyler: rollout plan? small region, 10k traces/day, measure billing delta vs baseline. if variance < 2% and tail errors manageable, expand.

Aisha: propose RFC + small staging experiment. I'll write RFC: outline (motivation, mapping algo, epoching, ingest changes, aggregator changes, retention + UX, rollout, risk matrix). volunteers: Tyler on ingest impl, Jin on late-enrich fallback, Ben on ops and SLO impacts, Maya on query/QA tooling, Elena on product messaging.

Ben (sre): add runbook item: how to revert if cohort mapping is skewed or a leak mixes tenants.

Aisha: good call, will add. target RFC by end of next week and experiment in staging 2 weeks after.

Elena (product): great — please @ me on the RFC so I can prep the customer-facing draft.

Aisha: will do. thanks all! :rocket:
